conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hello, I'm Dr. Lee. You're here today because your dialysis access isn't working well, correct?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, that's right. My peritoneal dialysis isn’t clearing my blood well anymore, and doing all these exchanges is exhausting.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand. You’ve been doing nightly cycler treatments plus two manual exchanges during the day. That’s a lot to manage.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. I’d really like to switch to hemodialysis if possible.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We can do that. You already have a left arm fistula from before your transplant, but the recent fistulogram showed poor blood flow and some blockages.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it’s not ready to use? I thought since it was there, it would just work.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s there, but the artery feeding it is narrowed, and there are side branches stealing blood flow. We need to fix that surgically.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will that make it usable for dialysis?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, the plan is to revise the fistula—ligate the side branches and re-route the blood flow so it works better for dialysis.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And this will be done today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, you’ll go to the operating room shortly. The surgeon will make sure your radial pulse stays intact and fix the inflow issue.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The surgery went well. They found the radial artery near the fistula was completely blocked, so they moved the inflow and tied off a large side branch.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is the fistula working now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: There’s a good thrill— that buzzing feeling—so blood is flowing well. That’s a great sign for future dialysis use.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m glad. I was worried it wouldn’t work after all this.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll monitor your hand overnight to make sure there’s no pain, numbness, or circulation issues. So far, everything looks stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. You’ve done well overnight—no complications. The dressing is clean, and we still hear a good bruit and feel the thrill.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So I can go home today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’re discharging you. You’ll go back to your regular peritoneal dialysis schedule for now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: When can I start using the fistula for hemodialysis?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It needs time to mature—usually 4 to 6 weeks. The access clinic will follow up to check readiness.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What should I watch for at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Call if you have fever, pain, numbness, or a cold or blue hand. Also, check daily for the thrill. If it’s gone, call immediately.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And I should keep the arm protected?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly—no blood pressures, no IVs, no heavy lifting, and avoid tight clothes or jewelry on that arm.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. Thank you for explaining everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Your medications stay the same, and the dressing comes off in a few days. Gentle washing is okay, but no soaking.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: All set. You’re cleared to go home. Follow up with the access clinic soon, and keep monitoring your fistula.
